newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas called flat to lower, cash firms.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas called flat to lower, cash firms.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures were expected to open unchanged to lower Tuesday despite early talk of stronger Gulf cash prices, market sources said.
June over-the-counter trade ranged from $2.27 to $2.285 after rallying Friday to settle at $2.285 per million British thermal units.
June is set to expire Wednesday.
Early cash prices at the Henry Hub, La., were talked about five cents higher at $2.25-2.27 as some unexpected loss of nuclear power tightened supplies in Texas and the Southwest.
Arizona Public Service shut the 1,221 megawatt (MW) Palo Verde 1 nuclear unit for repairs. A restart date was not yet known, the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) said.
Also, Texas Utilities cut power at its 1,150 MW Comanche Peak 2 unit to 47 percent to correct a vibration on a feedwater pump, the NRC report also stated.
Technically, traders said June support was at $2.15 and then at the $2.05 double bottom. Resistance was pegged at $2.30 and then at the $2.43 contract high.
In Friday's cash, Gulf Coast prices eased slightly to $2.14-2.19. Midcon pipes were off a few cents to the high-$1.90s, while New York city gate gas sold in the low-$2.40s.
Forecasts are calling for mostly below-normal temperatures across the eastern two thirds of the U.S. before moderating to near-normal by week's end, according to Weather Services Corp.
